coverage_gaps: Need primary-source market-cap, revenue mix, backlog, customer-concentration, and AI-exposure verification for every candidate before Layer 2 ranking.
Need non-U.S. ticker normalization and exchange-level validation for Japanese, Taiwanese, Korean, European, and Chinese substrate, OSAT, optics, and power-equipment suppliers.
Need more complete mapping of Korean HBM ecosystem suppliers, HBM test handlers, probe-card vendors, underfill/materials suppliers, and thermal-interface-material companies.

Need primary-source verification of optical substrate and precision materials candidates referenced by external research, including exact company identity, revenue growth, backlog, and qualification cycles.
Need market-pricing checks: current market capitalization, enterprise value, revenue multiple, analyst coverage count, short interest, ownership concentration, and recent 3/6/12-month price moves.
Need direct evidence to separate structural bottlenecks from cyclical rebounds, especially in ABF substrates, memory backend, optical components, EMS, and industrial electrical equipment.
Need falsification triggers for each node: lead-time compression, customer insourcing, capacity additions, margin pressure, inventory build, failed qualification, demand slowdown, or capex cuts.
Need customer dependency checks to avoid false positives where a supplier mentions AI but has immaterial or low-margin AI revenue exposure.

memory_update.text: AI Layer 1 universe should remain supply-chain-first: substrates, packaging, optics, power, cooling, and backend capacity can be more useful discovery lanes than obvious model or mega-cap software names.
ABF substrates and advanced PCB/interconnect remain the top Serenity bottleneck lane because of concentrated suppliers, long capacity lead times, and direct dependence by AI accelerators and servers.

Optical interconnect and photonics capacity should be kept as a separate AI chokepoint lane, with special attention to InP, lasers, photodetectors, precision substrates, qualification cycles, and alternative compound-semiconductor platforms.

HBM and AI accelerator demand may create backend packaging and testing overflow opportunities for OSATs and memory backend providers, but this requires primary-source validation of utilization, pricing, and customer mix.

Data-center power, switchgear, electrical balance-of-system, and thermal management should be included as underfollowed industrial AI lanes, but each candidate requires evidence that AI data centers are material to backlog and margins.

Layer 2 should prioritize primary-source validation and market-pricing checks for the highest-scoring underfollowed names: TTMI, Ibiden, Unimicron, ONTO, MKSI, Powertech, Camtek, Lumentum, Aeluma, Amtech, Powell, Modine, and nVent.

summary: Layer 1C merged the AI Layer 1 universe around physical AI infrastructure bottlenecks rather than only model, GPU, or hyperscaler leaders. The highest-priority lanes are advanced substrates/interconnect, advanced packaging and OSAT capacity, optical interconnect/photonics, HBM/memory backend overflow, data-center power and thermal infrastructure, grid/nuclear power supply, and niche AI automation/software. Reference leaders are retained as demand anchors, but the ranked universe deliberately favors underfollowed small/mid-cap, non-U.S.-listed, equipment, inspection, material, backend, and second-order suppliers whose AI relevance may be hidden inside supply-chain nodes. This is research support only and not a buy/sell recommendation.
